items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: this teacher, Miss Jordan, in the sixth grade. Miss Jordan played a very important part in my life... She was a very fine musician, also a school teacher.

ctx.x: (singing), 'Won't you be my sweet little household queen?' That's the way it ended up, see, as corny as it could be.

Anyhow, now I'm in the sixth grade -- this is a little later. We have a teacher called Miss Jordan. I'll never forget that. I went to 17th and Pine, to the public school now. My mother took me out of the Catholic school, 'cause she said all I was learning was the 'Hail Mary, full of grace', and she said, 'Look, son, I want you to know something about life. And I want you to meet the people that haven't been put in that condition.' So, what I said, I said to her, 'Well I will go, I want you to put me in this…

she'd line the class up and we'd sit there, and we'd say, now this is a singing period. And she would get her tuning fork, she'd give us the key by singing down, either from C down, or from te, do, te, la, or she'd be singing from do, mi, so, mi, and that'd be the key note. And so, all this was -- and then we'd go through and do it, she'd give us different parts and all like that. She was a very fine musician, also a school teacher.
